title: Trace Trellis — weekly capture + open floor
content:
Attendees: Maya C (owner), Arjun P, Lina G, Tomás R, Evelyn P, (drop-ins: SRE rotation: Noor)

Purpose: Weekly capture of ongoing tracing and dashboard work, quick sync on the KV-cache span-surge, open-floor for unblockers and pairing sessions. This is more of a freeform lab-notes doc than a polished playbook — capturing decisions and action items so we can drive tickets.

Top-line updates
- Span economy spike on 2026-11-07 (morning): 3x increase in span count for hosted-api-prod across model-cold-start requests. Root cause hypothesis: new rollout of model-shard-proxy v2 (PR linked) increases internal fan-out when prefix-kv cache miss occurs.
- Dashboard debt: low-cardinality metrics for prefix hits are present but not surfaced; users seeing noisy token-level graphs that burn query budget. We drafted a pruning plan.
- Sampling pilot: Arjun's mock for adaptive sampling based on trace-latency-percentile is ready to land in the canary namespace.

Notes from incident triage (span surge)
- Observed: increase in spans correlated with increased p99 latency by ~90ms for short chat RPCs during warmup windows.
- Timeline: 07:03 — model-shard-proxy v2 started 07:03:24; 07:03:32 — spike begins; 07:10 — autoscaler reacted and shed some backpressure.
- Quick root-hypothesis: v2 changed async fanout dispatch (now prints more internal child spans with unique ids). The increase is real span creation, not duplicate ingestion.
- Evidence: trace snippets show extra child spans in the worker dispatch path (worker/dispatch/async-run) flagged with new tag proxy.variant=v2.
- Temporary mitigation: added a short-lived enricher in the collector to drop spans with tag internal-proxy-debug=true (deploy ticket JIRA-OBS-4189) — reduces storage by ~46% in canary. Note: this masks data; not a long-term fix.

Decisions made
- Do not roll back model-shard-proxy v2 globally. The change has benefits for shard routing and will stay.
- We will modify the proxy to reduce debug-span fanout within the async dispatch path (owner: Arjun, target: 2026-11-13).
- Create a safe sampling policy that drops noisy internal spans by sampling key internal paths at 5% while keeping root RPCs at 100% (tmp plan to be documented in confluence).

Action items (owners and rough ETA)
- Arjun: Patch model-shard-proxy to gate internal fanout spans with a config flag and add telemetry counters for gated spans (JIRA-OBS-4123). ETA: 2026-11-13.
- Lina: Implement a dashboard that surfaces prefix-KV hit ratio, per-model prefix-hit latency and the token-query cost per route. This will be a condensed 1-pager dashboard in Grafana (panel mocks done). ETA: 2026-11-17.
- Tomás: Push sampling pilot to canary namespace, enable feature flag sampling.adaptive=true for 10% traffic. Collect 72h of signals and produce summary. ETA: 2026-11-16.
- Evelyn: Draft runbook appendix for span-surge detection and temporary mitigations. Include query templates to identify 'fanout smells'. ETA: 2026-11-12.
- Maya: Coordinate SRE on retention vs cost tradeoff, propose cold-path retention for internal spans to 3 days by default. ETA: 2026-11-20.

Sampling experiment details (Tomás)
- Goal: reduce disk/ingest costs by limiting internal-span volume while preserving enough traces for root-cause and latency SLO correlation.
- Approach: adaptive sampler that adjusts sample rate for internal-only traces based on 95th-percentile ingestion-volume window and p99-latency delta. Implementation notes: hook into collector pre-ingest; sampler state exposed to /metrics as sampling_rate_INTERNAL.
- Canary plan: start at 10% for internal spans for 24h, if dashboarded p99-latency-correlations remain stable, ramp to 25% for 48h. Abort if p99 latency correlations degrade by >5% or if error-tagged traces go up.

Dashboard pruning & cost telemetry (Lina)
- Problem: token-level dashboards for hosted-api are expensive to query and give little signal for prefix cache issues.
- Proposal: create an aggregated 'economics' dashboard that shows token-cost-per-route (derived), kv-prefix-hit-rate (aggregated by model, environment), and trace-ingest-rate with cost projection.
- Panels to build: 1) Prefix hit heatmap by model (7d), 2) Token-cost trend by route (30d), 3) Trace ingest delta vs billing (7d), 4) Low-cardinality alert for sudden drop in prefix-hit-rate.
- Data sources: traces->metrics pipeline (pre-aggregated increments) and billing export. Linked artifact: confluence page for dashboard schema.

Open-floor quick topics
- Noor (SRE): question about whether we should expose per-token cost to customers via console. Decision: product to own messaging; we will provide an internal API for cost signals. Link to product ticket later.
- Evelyn: noted we have no structured tests for sampling logic. Suggests adding unit tests for sampler thresholds + integration test in collector-catacomb infra. Approved.
- Maya: ask for pairing volunteers to reproduce a span that contains a large metadata blob (seen in sample trace id trace-20261107-9ab3). Volunteer: Tomás + Lina to pair on 2026-11-11 10:00 PT.

Risks and unknowns
- Masking spans at the collector reduces storage but increases chance of missing causal chains during complex incidents. Need to quantify diagnostic loss.
- Sampling introduces subtle biases in root-cause signal; we need to evaluate on at least two historical incidents.

Follow-up meeting schedule
- Quick sync next Monday 2026-11-16 09:30 PT — focused on sampling pilot results and deployment readiness.
- Pairing session 2026-11-11 10:00 PT (Tomás + Lina) to reproduce large metadata-span.

Notes/to-self (informal)
- Keep spike notes short and put longer writeup into confluence once we confirm hypothesis.
- Slack thread to continue: #obs-traces -> thread pinned: 'fanout spike 2026-11-07' (slack link above).
- Possible follow-up: cost simulation to show impact of reducing internal-span retention from 30 days -> 3 days for internal-only traces (Maya to run a projection using Nov billing export).

Appendix: quick query snippets (for triage)
- Find traces with proxy.variant=v2 and internal child spans > 5: 
  - trace query: tag=proxy.variant:v2 AND count(child.span) > 5 AND service=worker-dispatch
- Estimate disk impact for a timespan: use billing export query + trace_ingest_bytes grouped by env/model

End of notes — will iterate. If you add more experimental results, paste them below (keep date stamp).
